summary.headline: The Planning Board reviewed lighting, landscaping and stormwater plans for the proposed Costco project and approved scenic road tree removals.
summary.summary: The Planning Board conducted an extensive technical review of the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco wholesale club at 21 Coslin Drive, focusing on exterior lighting, native landscaping compliance, and stormwater drainage systems. The board also held a scenic road public hearing and approved removing hazardous public shade trees across town after altering one recommendation based on a resident's safety concern. Additionally, members continued the MBTA Communities housing proposal for 0 Southville Road and discussed draft zoning bylaw amendments intended for the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

topics.title: 21 Coslin Drive (Costco): Lighting, landscaping and utilities review
topics.summary: Representatives for Costco presented detailed plans for the proposed 167,000-square-foot store and 895-space parking lot at the Southborough-Westborough line. The discussion covered 36.6-foot light poles approved by the Zoning Board of Appeals, dark-sky lighting fixtures, and proposed landscaping with 256 deciduous trees, 120 evergreen trees, and over 1,200 shrubs. The applicant requested waivers for cool-season turf grass, rock mulch in parking islands, and stormwater infiltration standards due to site soil constraints, while highlighting a 15,000-square-foot net reduction in impervious surface.
key_details: Light poles stand at 36.6 feet under a prior variance, utilizing 3,000-Kelvin dark-sky compliant LED fixtures that dim significantly one hour after store closing.
Total site plantings across Southborough and Westborough include 256 deciduous trees, 120 evergreens, 1,272 shrubs, 447 groundcover junipers, and 361 grasses.
Costco requested waivers to use rock mulch near buildings and parking islands to reduce fire hazards, and filter fabric on steep slopes for erosion control.
The stormwater system includes two above-ground wetland detention ponds and an underground infiltration chamber designed to contain a 100-year storm event.
Sanitary sewage of up to 15,000 gallons per day will route via gravity into an existing 50,000-gallon pump station and pump across Route 9 to Westborough.
topics.outcome: Continued the public hearing to December 14, 2026, and extended the board's decision deadline to December 18, 2026.
topics.why_it_matters: The regional warehouse project will alter traffic, lighting, and environmental runoff at the town boundary and represents a major commercial development in Southborough.

topics.title: Scenic road public shade tree removal hearing
topics.summary: The board and the tree warden held a joint hearing on a Department of Public Works petition to address 24 trees along designated scenic roads. Most trees were dead or dying ash, oak, maple, and pine trees ranging from 12 to 54 inches in diameter. After hearing concerns from an abutter about an unstable locust tree leaning over power lines and a home, the board agreed to change its recommendation from trimming to full removal.
key_details: The list originally recommended 22 tree removals and two trimmings across roads including Breakneck Hill, Clemmons, Edgewood, and Pine Hill.
A resident of 3 Pine Hill Road requested full removal of a rotting locust tree; the tree warden and board agreed to remove rather than trim it.
A resident of 22 Breakneck Hill Road supported the planned heavy trimming of an oak tree leaning toward their home to rebalance its canopy weight.
Tree contractor work for the most critical trees was scheduled to begin immediately, with the remainder addressed over the winter.
topics.outcome: Approved the tree removal list with the amendment changing 3 Pine Hill Road from trimming to removal, then closed the hearing.

topics.title: 0 Southville Road: MBTA Communities development continuance
topics.summary: The board formally opened the public hearing for an application under the MBTA Communities Overlay District proposing 60 apartment-style dwelling units across two buildings with a clubhouse and 110 parking spaces at 0 Southville Road. The applicant requested a continuance without testimony to resolve questions with public safety officials before presenting.
key_details: The project proposes 60 units on parcel 5-8 at 9 Southville Road with two waivers for parking located in front yards and within setbacks.
The applicant requested additional time to coordinate with town public safety officials.
No testimony was taken during the meeting.
topics.outcome: Continued the public hearing without testimony to December 14, 2026 at 6:45 PM.

topics.title: ZBA proposed zoning bylaw amendments for 2027 Town Meeting
topics.summary: Zoning Board of Appeals members presented draft zoning bylaw amendments intended to align town bylaws with recent amendments to the Massachusetts Zoning Act (MGL Chapter 40A). Planning Board members reviewed proposed changes to sections governing non-conforming structures and undersized lots, urging caution to ensure local wording does not inadvertently expand development rights or exceed state mandates.
key_details: The amendments respond to statewide statutory changes adopted during the previous legislative session.

Planning Board members raised concerns that deleting 'single or two-family' phrasing in Section 174-19.B could unintentionally grant broader expansion rights to commercial or non-conforming structures.
Members highlighted the need to preserve protections under Section 174-17 regarding dimensional non-conformities and side and rear setbacks.
ZBA representatives and planning members agreed to collaborate on refined draft language before the formal public hearing.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; a formal Planning Board public hearing on the proposed zoning articles is set for December 14, 2026.
topics.why_it_matters: Zoning bylaw amendments directly govern what property owners can build or expand on non-conforming lots across town and must be approved by voters at Town Meeting.

topics.title: FY26 open space monitoring report presentation
topics.summary: Joseph Orzel of Lucas Environmental presented the annual monitoring report on deeded open space parcels and easements across six subdivisions. The survey identified common encroachments such as yard waste piles and invasive plants, as well as specific issues including an unpermitted shed inside an easement at Fisher Road Estates and a historically resolved home encroachment at Presidential Estates. The board agreed to send educational and corrective letters to affected property owners.
key_details: Six subdivision open spaces were inspected: Vale Terrace, Woodbury at Southborough, Fisher Road Estates, Presidential Estates, Pine Hill Estates, and Rubie Estates.
Yard waste, grass clippings, and brush piles were the most frequent violations found in open space buffers.
At Fisher Road Estates (Andrews Way), several encroachments including lawn expansion, fencing, and a shed were found in the 30-foot open space easement.
The chair confirmed that lots 3B-1 and 7 at Vale Terrace had previously been transferred to the care and custody of the Conservation Commission.
At Presidential Estates (3 Glenwood Road), past home construction inside open space had been resolved via a land swap granting alternate open space.
topics.outcome: Board accepted the report findings and directed staff to issue informational letters to abutters violating open space easements.

topics.title: Routine business: Town planner updates and minutes
topics.summary: The town planner gave updates on ongoing committee work, including drafting a modified 55-plus housing bylaw with the Affordable Housing Trust for Town Meeting consideration in spring 2027. The board reviewed and approved meeting minutes from November 2, 2026, and January 7, 2026.
key_details: The Affordable Housing Trust and town staff are refining the 55-plus housing bylaw, with a presentation planned for December 14 and hearings in January 2027.
A proposed warrant article correcting industrial zone uses will also be submitted for Town Meeting.
Minutes of November 2, 2026, were approved as amended.
Minutes of January 7, 2026, were approved as drafted with two abstentions.
topics.outcome: Meeting minutes approved; meeting adjourned at approximately 9:34 PM.

votes.motion: Continue the public hearing for major site plan approval, highway business retail special permit, and lower impact development special permit for 21 Coslin Drive to December 14, 2026, at 6:30 PM.
Extend the decision due date for 21 Coslin Drive to December 18, 2026.
Accept the scenic road tree removal list from the Department of Public Works dated October 2026 with the exception of tree SO8 at 3 Pine Hill Road, changing it from trimming to removal.
Close the public hearing on the scenic road tree removal list.
Continue the public hearing for 0 Southville Road major site plan approval under the MBTA Communities overlay district without testimony to December 14, 2026, at 6:45 PM.

public_comment.summary: A Southborough resident and former Open Space Preservation Commission chair commended Costco for committing to straight native species but cautioned against using landscape fabric and rock mulch in parking islands, explaining that rock surfaces heat soil, impede burrowing native bees and fireflies, and fail to provide the ecological benefits of organic groundcover.

A resident of 3 Pine Hill Road requested that a damaged locust tree near his driveway and power lines be fully removed rather than trimmed, citing rot at the tree base and recent history of trees falling and causing property damage and power outages on the street.

A resident of 22 Breakneck Hill Road inquired why an oak tree in front of their home was designated for trimming rather than removal given its severe lean toward the house, but accepted the tree warden's plan to prune house-facing limbs to rebalance the tree's weight toward the street.

upcoming.what: Continued public hearings on 21 Coslin Drive (Costco) traffic review and 0 Southville Road MBTA development, plus public hearing on ZBA zoning amendments
